_comment: How a word of a text in Levantine Arabic is turned into something a dictionary can be asked about: the Levantine dictionary first (kaikki's South and North Levantine Arabic), the standard one after it, these rules and then lib/lang/ar.lookup.json's. Written onto a word standard Arabic also has: the present's b- (بيكتب, بحكي = أحكي), the future's ḥa- (حيروح; رح is a word of its own), the demonstrative and the preposition fused with the article (هالبيت = هذا البيت, عالطاولة = على الطاولة), the pronoun written onto the verb with -l- (قلّي, احكيلو), the negation's -š (مابعرفش) and the dropped hamza. Measured on TODOs/arabic-dialects/ar-lev.txt.

_article: THE ARTICLE IS TAKEN OFF HERE and not in ar.lookup.json: Wiktionary's standard Arabic files a word with its article among its forms, and its dialect dictionaries do not (الولاد, الدراري, للدار found nothing). A verb's prefix leaves three letters at least (`min_stem_length`): حالك is not the future's ح + الك.
